scenario.name: Test: distcc NOT remotely exploitable (tier-3 negative case)
scenario.author: Thomas Shaw
scenario.description: Negative control for the agentic pipeline's tier-3 (exploit) testing (Phase 1C). Identical to test_scenario_distcc — a Debian 12 target running the vulnerable DistCC daemon (CVE-2004-2687) and a Kali/MSF attacker on one private network — except the target also runs an iptables rule that drops the attacker's traffic to distcc's port (3632). distccd is still installed (tier 1) and still listening locally (tier 2, detected via the listening socket), but the Metasploit exploit from the attacker cannot reach it, so the distcc_exec module's tier-3 test_msf_exploit check must report FAIL, not a false PASS. This proves the tier-3 check is a real exploit test, not a rubber stamp. Both systems share a 10.90.0.0/24 private network (logical VLAN 1): IP_addresses[0] 10.90.0.10 is the target, [1] 10.90.0.20 is the attacker.
